Issues.Title: Replace PR reviewer orchestration with a frozen review bundle
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Replaces the orchestration-heavy `review-pull-request` skill (supersedes #69467) with a simpler design:

- **`scripts/prepare-review.mjs`** is a trusted producer. It:
  - freezes the PR's head, merge base, and base tip;
  - fetches the authoritative diff and existing feedback;
  - routes guides with the existing routing rules, including renames via `previous_filename`;
  - writes a frozen review bundle with a v2 manifest.

  Reviewer guidance comes from a selected trusted source: the local checkout when run interactively, or the workflow's own commit when hosted. It never comes from the target release branch or from PR-controlled content. Every link found in a guide is classified and recorded:
  - policy sections are included as review criteria;
  - architecture documents are included as orientation-only context;
  - all other links are recorded as skipped.

  The repository's "Security Concerns Are Out of Scope" exclusion is carried over verbatim.
- **`SKILL.md`** is now a review-only contract (144 lines):
  - a one-line local bootstrap;
  - one worker per routed guide;
  - `BLOCKED` / `INCOMPLETE` / `NO_FINDINGS` results, with every guide marked `complete`, `incomplete`, or `excluded`;
  - a requirement to read the full callee body before accepting or discarding a claim.
- **`pull-request-review.md` (gh-aw)** runs the same producer, downloaded at `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA`, when `/review` is requested and before the agent starts. The agent has no GitHub tools and reads only from the bundle. A trusted `verify_live_head` job must pass before `safe_outputs` publishes a COMMENT-only review pinned to the frozen head. Recompiled with gh-aw v0.88.7 `--strict`.

This fixes the original failure where release branches that predate the shared guides, such as `release/11.0`, could not be reviewed. There is no automatic fallback to `main`, local files, or the PR head.

Guide routing is still hard-coded to the two existing guides: CrossCutting always, plus BlazorComponents for `src/Components` / `src/JSInterop`. New architecture documents are supporting context and do not require new routing; a new review guide would.

## Validation

**Producer tests:** 32/32 passing. They cover routing, link classification, renames, mixed-line policies, exclusions, and malformed or empty inputs.

**Offline evaluation** (planted bugs on fixture branches):
- the planted bugs were found on the `main` and `release/11.0`-era fixtures;
- a known false null-reference claim was rejected after reading the actual helper body;
- the docs-only case (#69330) returned NO_FINDINGS with all 14 topics accounted for.

**Hosted, on a fork only:** three positive/control pairs, two on `main` and one on a `release/11.0`-era base. Each positive published its planted finding on the correct line at the frozen head, and each control completed with no findings.

**Local native invocation (passed):** on the open `release/11.0` PR #68895 at `3f7c176`:
- the skill ran the bootstrap itself (41 s);
- guidance came from a clean local commit;
- both per-guide workers completed, with result `FINDINGS` (one source-only finding, not published);
- nothing was published and the checkout was left clean.

**Moved head, end-of-run gate (passed):** fork run 36085449165.
- The head moved from `9c69c746` to `c081fe3` while the agent was running.
- The agent staged a review, then `verify_live_head` failed and `safe_outputs` was skipped.
- Nothing was published.

A first attempt, run 36084564466, moved the head during preparation instead. The producer blocked it before the agent started, which exercises only the pre-agent check.

**Incomplete signal (partial):** fork run 36084877338, using a validation-only variant. One `report_incomplete` was emitted, and zero reviews, comments, or issues were created. No worker ran, so this does **not** show that a valid finding is held back after partial worker completion.

Planted fixtures show the design works on those cases; they do not establish broad review accuracy.

## Known limitation: external contracts

Reviewers read only the frozen bundle, so they cannot cite primary external contracts such as the WHATWG HTML or Streams specs, or `dotnet/runtime` source. Findings that depend on one are reported as unresolved or incomplete rather than guessed.

- **Locally:** main's reviewer can fetch specs today, so this PR occasionally misses what main catches. For example, main accepted the case-sensitive `VALUE` issue on #67616 using the WHATWG attribute-name contract; this reviewer rejected it.
- **Hosted:** a review that needs a spec publishes nothing.

Allowing primary-spec evidence (and, for hosted, a network allowlist) is a permission decision deferred to a follow-up PR.

## Follow-ups before leaving draft

- Independent feedback from local runs on real PRs.
- Suppression of a valid finding when one guide is incomplete (not yet tested).
- Hosted coverage:
  - docs-only, JSInterop-only, and large PRs;
  - community fork PRs;
  - the upstream repository environment;
  - bundle size (0.5–0.8 GB currently, 40–60 s to prepare).
- Minor friction: `SKILL.md` should state that bundle files carry a `.source` suffix.
- A possible gap: architecture documents reach workers only when a routed guide links to them.

No product code changes.

Issues.Title: Blazor Virtualize can use a disposed DotNetObjectReference during rapid navigation
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

When rapidly switching between pages that contain `Virtualize` controls in a Blazor Server app, `Virtualize<TItem>.OnAfterRenderAsync` can attempt to pass a disposed `DotNetObjectReference<VirtualizeJsInterop>` to JS interop. This results in an unhandled circuit exception and terminates the circuit.

This appears to be a race between component disposal during navigation and the asynchronous post-render JS interop initialization.

### Expected Behavior

Navigating away from a page containing a `Virtualize` control should not invoke JS interop with an already-disposed object reference or terminate the circuit.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run a Blazor Server app with multiple pages containing `Virtualize` controls.
2. Rapidly switch between those pages.
3. Observe an intermittent `ObjectDisposedException` from `Virtualize<TItem>.OnAfterRenderAsync`.

### Exceptions (if any)

```text
fail: Aspire.Hosting.Dashboard.ThirdParty.Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits.CircuitHost[111]
      Unhandled exception in circuit 'SZDv3NEsrcPjLELTrbC1H1U2JHCS79fVHFMtRyzM_xA'.
      System.ObjectDisposedException: Cannot access a disposed object.
      Object name: 'Microsoft.JSInterop.DotNetObjectReference`1[[Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web.Virtualization.VirtualizeJsInterop, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web, Version=11.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=adb9793829ddae60]]'.
         at Microsoft.JSInterop.JSRuntime.TrackObjectReference[TValue](DotNetObjectReference`1 dotNetObjectReference)
         at System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonConverter`1.TryWrite(Utf8JsonWriter writer, T& value, JsonSerializerOptions options, WriteStack& state)
         at System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonCollectionConverter`2.OnTryWrite(Utf8JsonWriter writer, TCollection value, JsonSerializerOptions options, WriteStack& state)
         at System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonConverter`1.WriteCore(Utf8JsonWriter writer, T& value, JsonSerializerOptions options, WriteStack& state)
         at Microsoft.JSInterop.JSRuntime.InvokeAsync[TValue](Int64 targetInstanceId, String identifier, JSCallType callType, CancellationToken cancellationToken, Object[] args)
         at Microsoft.JSInterop.JSRuntime.InvokeAsync[TValue](Int64 targetInstanceId, String identifier, JSCallType callType, Object[] args)
         at Microsoft.JSInterop.JSRuntimeExtensions.InvokeVoidAsync(IJSRuntime jsRuntime, String identifier, Object[] args)
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web.Virtualization.Virtualize`1.OnAfterRenderAsync(Boolean firstRender)
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.RenderTree.Renderer.GetErrorHandledTask(Task taskToHandle, ComponentState owningComponentState)
```

### .NET Version

ASP.NET Core 11.0 prerelease (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web, Version=11.0.0.0`).

### Anything else?

Originally observed in the Aspire dashboard, where the logger category is prefixed with `Aspire.Hosting.Dashboard.ThirdParty`. The exception itself originates from Blazor's `Virtualize<TItem>` implementation.

Issues.Title: Add focused read-only issue investigation skill
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Add a small, public, read-only `investigate-issue` skill for one unfixed ASP.NET Core issue. It checks for existing fixes first, starts with the reporter's goal, compares source behavior with documented contracts and tests, and identifies the evidence needed when a conclusion remains uncertain.

This narrower replacement for #69028 contains only the skill. It does not include the earlier PR's evaluation framework, Docker worker, workflow, or persistence infrastructure. Optional execution requires concrete approval and a suitable existing disposable environment; the skill provides no runner.

## Investigation evidence

The three issue assessments below were **manual follows** of the skill text. Separately, a fresh Copilot CLI session **invoked the current project skill** on #67911 and stopped at its existing-fix rule; an earlier CLI session invoked the preceding revision on #69485. Current `SKILL.md` SHA-256: `6a7969f6e8a08e3fde9d896d93fb68496e855cac38f8176f5ddf60ecc48fc1f8`. Invocation verifies that the skill loads, not that it improves accuracy or saves time.

### #69485 — Vue SPA asset caching

- **Source finding:** `MapFallbackToFile("index.html")` serves `/` through [static-file middleware](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/a58827bd1ee664f61214baf006370254a5209954/src/Middleware/StaticFiles/src/StaticFilesEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L180-L205), not a `MapStaticAssets` manifest endpoint. The [.NET 10.0.400 SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v10.0.400/src/StaticWebAssetsSdk/Tasks/DefineStaticWebAssetEndpoints.cs#L119-L165) assigns immutable caching to a generated SDK fingerprint token, not merely a Vite filename that looks hashed. Its [mapping matcher uses the basename](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v10.0.400/src/StaticWebAssetsSdk/Tasks/Data/ContentTypeProvider.cs#L420-L475), so the reported `assets\*.*` pattern cannot match that JS filename.
- **Controlled runtime check (not the reporter's app):** Published a first-party `dotnet new web` app with SDK **10.0.400** in an offline, disposable Linux/arm64 container. It used `app.MapStaticAssets(); app.MapFallbackToFile("index.html");`, a 2,223-byte `wwwroot/index.html`, `wwwroot/assets/index-DAMbWbfh.js`, and the two project-file mappings from the issue. In Production, requests with `Accept-Encoding: br, gzip` returned:

  | Request | Status | `Cache-Control` | `Content-Encoding` |
  | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
  | `/` (fallback) | 200 | absent | absent; 2,223 bytes |
  | `/index.html` (manifest endpoint) | 200 | `no-cache` | `br`; 184 bytes |
  | `/assets/index-DAMbWbfh.js` (original URL) | 200 | `no-cache` | `br`; 51 bytes |

  The published manifest had **no `fingerprint` property on the original JS route**; it also generated a *different*, SDK-fingerprinted JS route with `max-age=31536000, immutable`. Two clean-rebuilt controls changed only the project's mapping items: adding `Pattern="index-*.js" Priority="100"` still selected built-in `*.js` and kept the original JS route at `no-cache`; adding `Pattern="index-DAMbWbfh.js" Priority="100"` selected that exact pattern and returned `public, max-age=604800, immutable` on the original JS route. The latter is a scoped control, not a general solution for changing Vite filenames.
- **Next evidence and limit:** Obtain the reporter's actual `Program.cs`, published endpoint manifest, environment, and raw response headers for `/`, `/index.html`, and the JS URL. This controlled app establishes the platform behavior for **its** configuration, not a reproduction of their deployment or a warranted framework-fix difficulty rating. No reporter app was run; the preceding-revision CLI investigation was source-only.

### #69157 — validation on an inherited record property

- **Finding:** The issue's constructor is named `AffectedRequest` inside `CDerived`, so the supplied snippet cannot compile as written. In public main, record constructor selection can [match an inherited property](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/a58827bd1ee664f61214baf006370254a5209954/src/Validation/gen/Parsers/ValidationsGenerator.TypesParser.cs#L215-L227), but [member extraction searches only the derived type's members](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/a58827bd1ee664f61214baf006370254a5209954/src/Validation/gen/Parsers/ValidationsGenerator.TypesParser.cs#L230-L291). The [attribute lookup uses the property's declaring type](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/a58827bd1ee664f61214baf006370254a5209954/src/Validation/gen/Emitters/ValidationsGenerator.Emitter.cs#L135-L189), so changing just the lookup would still lose `[Range]` on the derived constructor parameter.
- **Next evidence:** Correct the snippet and check the .NET version and `AddValidation()` setup. Run an actual JSON endpoint with invalid and valid `n` and a base-property-annotation control to distinguish binding from validation.
- **Limit:** This is a source-level hypothesis, not an observed runtime failure or an explicit contract for this shape. Fix difficulty is provisionally **Medium only if the behavior is supported and reproduced**.

### #67911 — OutputCache entry-size accounting

- **Finding:** Active, unmerged [PR #68742](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/68742) explicitly addresses the reported missing cache-key size and changes the memory store and its tests. The skill's first-step rule correctly **stops at an applicable fix**, without reviewing the PR implementation or repeating the diagnosis.
- **Next action:** Follow that PR through review and integration.
- **Limit:** Its correctness and release disposition are unverified; no independent fix-difficulty rating was assigned. The current-revision CLI invocation exercised this stopping rule.

### Separate #66553 browser pilot

A **manual skill follow**, not either CLI invocation: a published .NET 10 MVC app in one Chromium 154 setup made **two HTTP 200 GETs** for a fingerprinted entry module with generated import-map integrity metadata and an external module `src`. Removing the map's integrity property or using an inline import yielded **one GET**; the script executed once in every case. See the [reporter issue](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/66553) and [import-map implementation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/02cb50575506b0cd5aae4d96fd3ee4c29f469472/src/Components/Endpoints/src/Assets/ImportMapDefinition.cs). The next checks are serving identical HTML from a simple static server and adding matching integrity on the external entry tag while retaining the map. This one-browser result does not establish framework responsibility or a fix; the local browser trace is not attached here.

## Scope and previous feedback

The skill incorporates an existing-fix check, begins with the reporter's goal, compares behavior with contract evidence, and preserves the trigger in any reduction. It addresses missing facts and product responsibility at a general level. It does **not** claim exhaustive request-type guidance, a fixed report template, a supplied execution environment, or an evaluation harness; those broader concerns remain outside this focused change.

No reporter-provided code was executed in the three source-only issue assessments or the separate first-party #69485 probe. No issue, label, or project state was changed by the investigations. These examples show bounded uncertainty reduction and an appropriate early stop—not measured productivity or independently verified framework fixes. Feedback on whether this helps maintainers decide what to do next is welcome.

Issues.Title: Expose the daily PR Attention Pulse JSON snapshot
Issues.Body:
## Description

Follow-up to #69355, based on `main` with #69415. This change is independent of #69492.

- Add a compact Snapshot section to the canonical Pulse report with a frozen UTC generation time, producing run/attempt link, artifact/file names, and the SHA-256 of the exact exported JSON bytes.
- Freeze Actions-derived identity privately before inference, keep the model-visible three-file allowlist unchanged, and have the private validator independently verify the context, checksum, and exact regenerated report.
- Reuse the non-overwriting `pulse-publication-evidence` artifact and seven-day retention. Preserve the capped schema `2.0.0` JSON bytes, classifications, caps, ordering, sole issue-body replacement, publication gates, permissions, and pinned tooling.
- Document the JSON contract and authenticated retrieval by the identity in the published report, including pagination, duplicate/rerun ambiguity, checksum verification, early deletion, and expiry. This does not export the full queue or add a canvas, service, or storage layer.
- Adversarial-review follow-up: fail retrieval when a downloaded ZIP or entry cannot be read, even if another artifact matches. Keep fully inspected nonmatches and expired-artifact handling unchanged; cover both candidate orders.

## Validation

Using the existing gh-aw v0.88.7 installation:

- `pwsh -NoProfile -File .github\workflows\pr-attention-pulse-tests\Test-PulseSnapshotRetrieval.ps1` — 90/90 local consumer cases passed after the review fix. All four new archive/entry-read rows failed for the expected reason before the fix and passed afterward.
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File .github\workflows\pr-attention-pulse\Compile-PRAttentionPulse.ps1` — succeeded with zero warnings after the review fix.
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File .github\workflows\pr-attention-pulse\Compile-PRAttentionPulse.ps1 -Validate` — succeeded with zero warnings after the review fix.
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File .github\workflows\pr-attention-pulse-tests\Test-PRAttentionPulse.ps1` — full local suite passed after the review fix. This includes `Test-PulseSnapshot.ps1` (82 snapshot cases), 91 retrieval cases including the producer-to-documented-consumer pair, the real pinned publication handler with mocked GitHub transport, review/merge/comment controls, schedule checks, generated controls, and presentation goldens across three cultures.
- Thirteen per-case behavioral baseline failures became green; ten discriminating mutations were detected. New interfaces unavailable on the baseline were recorded as limitations rather than counted as behavioral failures.
- `git -c core.longpaths=true diff --check` — clean. Queue producer, sanitizer, combiner, shared action lock, and non-agent generated jobs remained unchanged. The review fix changes only the consumer example and its regression tests.

## Boundaries

Validation is local and fixture-based. No hosted Pulse dispatch, live collection/inference, live artifact retrieval, or dashboard issue update was performed. Reruns or deletion may make referenced artifacts unavailable before retention expires; consumers must not substitute a newer unpublished run or attempt.

Issues.Title: Improve contributor guidance for fresh worktrees and fatal test-host failures
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Document several repeatable setup and validation steps that are currently discoverable only after targeted Components builds or tests fail in a fresh worktree.

These additions would help contributors and coding agents distinguish environment/bootstrap failures from product failures and preserve useful diagnostics when a regression terminates the test host.

## Proposed improvements

### Repository test guidance

Add guidance for regressions whose expected failure terminates the test host:

- Run the normal repository build/test command first so the supported path is exercised.
- If the wrapper reports the process failure but does not preserve the fatal child-process output, rerun the already-built test assembly directly with the same runner and test filter.
- Redirect that output to a diagnostic artifact and record the exit code, fatal message, and relevant call-chain frames.
- Continue to use the normal repository command for green-path verification; direct runner invocation is diagnostic evidence, not a replacement for the supported build/test flow.

### Fresh Windows worktree bootstrap

Document that a targeted build can fail before compilation when generated repository imports have not been created yet.

When `artifacts\bin\GenerateFiles\Directory.Build.props` is missing, contributors should:

1. Activate the repository-local .NET environment with `. .\activate.ps1`.
2. Run `.\restore.cmd` once from the repository root.
3. Retry the original targeted command unchanged.

This should be described as a worktree bootstrap condition rather than a product-build failure.

### Components E2E prerequisite

Document the existing recovery step when the Components E2E build reports that MessagePack-CSharp source files are missing:

```powershell
git submodule update --init src\submodules\MessagePack-CSharp
```

After initialization, contributors should rerun the same dependency-aware E2E build rather than altering project references or build properties.

### Static web assets with NodeJS disabled

Document the targeted recovery for a missing `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Internal.Assets` `staticwebassets.build.json` when `BuildNodeJS=false`.

The assets project has `DefaultTargets="Pack"`, which can leave the build manifest absent in this configuration. Build it explicitly once per active configuration:

```powershell
. .\activate.ps1
dotnet build src\Assets\Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Internal.Assets.csproj `
  -t:Build `
  -v:q `
  -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false `
  -p:BuildNodeJS=false
```

Use `-c Release` for Release validation, then retry the original targeted test command.

## Suggested locations

- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`: fatal test-host diagnostic guidance.
- `src/Components/AGENTS.md`: fresh-worktree bootstrap, MessagePack-CSharp E2E prerequisite, and static-web-assets recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fresh-worktree targeted Components builds have a documented recovery path for missing generated repository imports.
- Components E2E builds have a documented recovery path for an uninitialized MessagePack-CSharp submodule.
- Debug and Release targeted builds document the explicit static-assets build required when NodeJS is disabled and the manifest is absent.
- Regressions that terminate the test host have a documented way to preserve fatal output without replacing the supported green-path test command.
- The guidance avoids issue-specific test names or implementation details and remains reusable across Components investigations.

Issues.Title: Document source-generator wiring and build-gate gotchas in agent instruction files
Issues.Body:
## Summary

While working in `src/Components/Testing` (#67083), several repository behaviors cost significant debugging time because they are not captured in any `AGENTS.md` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Each one produced errors whose message pointed away from the actual cause, which is exactly the failure mode agent instructions are meant to prevent.

All claims below were re-verified against `main` at `a58827bd1e`. Line numbers refer to that commit.

## 1. Analyzer `ProjectReference` must stay in the consuming project file

**Proposed location:** new section in `src/Components/Testing/AGENTS.md`.

`eng/targets/ResolveReferences.targets:101` re-materializes the `ProjectReference` set while resolving `Reference` items:

```xml
<ProjectReference Include="@(Reference->Distinct()->'%(ProjectPath)')" />
```

An `OutputItemType="Analyzer"` `ProjectReference` contributed from a `Directory.Build.props` is silently discarded by this rewrite. The generator then emits nothing, and the failure surfaces as errors that look unrelated to build wiring — in our case `MSTEST0030` (no `[TestClass]` found) plus `CS0119`, neither of which mentions analyzers or generators.

**Why this is worth writing down now:** `main` has four copies of this same reference block, in `src/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing.csproj:53`, `testassets/TestApp.E2E.Tests/TestApp.E2E.Tests.csproj:52`, `testassets/NativeAotTestApp/NativeAotTestApp.csproj:90`, and `testassets/NativeAotTestApp.E2E.Tests/NativeAotTestApp.E2E.Tests.csproj:41`. `src/Components/Testing/testassets/Directory.Build.props` already exists and is the obvious place to deduplicate them. Only one of the four sites carries an explanatory comment, and none warns against relocating the item — so the refactor is both tempting and silently breaking.

Suggested guidance: apply the generator as an analyzer from the consuming project file itself; never hoist it into a props file; verify the item survives evaluation with `dotnet build <project> --getItem:ProjectReference`, noting that `OutputItemType` items only materialize during a real build.

## 2. Do not use repo-wide `EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles` to inspect generated code

**Proposed location:** same new section.

Setting `-p:EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles=true` together with a global `CompilerGeneratedFilesOutputPath` flows into every transitively built project. Unrelated generators re-emit their sources, producing spurious `CS0757` (duplicate partial method) failures in projects untouched by the change, and leaving stray `obj/gen-out` folders across the tree. Both properties must be scoped to the single project under investigation.

No `.md` in the repository currently mentions either property.

## 3. Implicit usings + build-time code style enforcement

**Proposed location:** `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `### Formatting`.

Verified in `eng/targets/CSharp.Common.targets`:

- `:35` — `IDE0005` is suppressed **only** when `TargetFrameworks` (plural) is set, so it is live for single-TFM projects.
- `:44` — `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` defaults to `true`.
- `:51-53` — implicit usings are enabled when `TargetFrameworks` is empty and `TargetFramework == $(DefaultNetCoreTargetFramework)`.
- `:56-60` — `System.Linq` is removed for src projects, `System.Net.Http` is removed everywhere, and `Xunit` is added for test projects.

Net effect: hand-adding `using System;`, `using System.Collections.Generic;`, or `using System.Threading.Tasks;` to a single-TFM project **fails the build** rather than warning. This bit us twice in one change. Conversely `System.Linq` (src) and `System.Net.Http` still need explicit directives.

Note: `.editorconfig:279` sets `IDE0005.severity = warning`, yet a plain `dotnet build -c Release` reported `error IDE0005`. The exact escalation mechanism was not pinned down, so any wording should stay empirical ("fails the build") rather than naming a specific property.

## 4. `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` is a two-way build gate

**Proposed location:** `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `## Public API Changes`. **Lowest value of the four** — the existing bullet already mentions the file, but only in terms of API-review semantics, not the mechanical gate.

The only unstated point: the analyzer fails the build in both directions, so *removing* a member or reducing accessibility requires deleting its baseline entries, just as adding one requires new entries. Reasonable to fold into the existing bullet or skip entirely.

## 5. Correction: the blanket xUnit statement is now inaccurate

`.github/copilot-instructions.md:53` states flatly:

> We use xUnit SDK v3 for tests.

`src/Components/Testing` is **mixed**, which my original framing got wrong and is worth stating precisely:

- `test/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing.Tests.csproj` — xUnit v3.
- `testassets/TestApp.E2E.Tests`, `testassets/NativeAotTestApp.E2E.Tests`, `testassets/PackageConsumer/Tests` — MSTest on Microsoft.Testing.Platform (`EnableMSTestRunner`).

This interacts with item 3: `CSharp.Common.targets:59` implicitly adds `using Xunit` to every project where `IsTestProject` is true, while MSTest injects `Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting` when implicit usings are on. The two collide on `Assert` and `TestContext`, which is why the unit-test project has to set `ImplicitUsings=disable` — see the comment at `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing.Tests.csproj:19-22`.

Line 51 already says "Follow the containing project's test framework", which partly mitigates this, but it directly contradicts line 53. The risk is an agent "helpfully" converting MSTest tests back to xUnit, or fighting the implicit `using Xunit` in an MSTest project. Suggest qualifying line 53 rather than leaving the flat claim.

## Minor

`## Running tests` (line 60) prescribes `./src/Http/build.sh -test`, which is Linux-only; `src/Components/AGENTS.md` carries richer Windows guidance. Worth a cross-reference, though this is cosmetic.

## Deliberately not proposed

`src/Components/Testing/AGENTS.md` already covers the public-API-minimization lesson from this work ("Hide storage layout, path composition, build plumbing, and other implementation details unless customers need to control them directly"), so no addition is proposed there. Items 1 and 2 are proposed as a **new** section rather than edits to existing content, since they cover generator wiring, which that file does not currently discuss.

---

Happy to open a PR with the wording above if the direction looks right.

Issues.Title: `EF Core UserStore.CreateUserPasskey` does not set `Aaguid`, so it's lost on passkey creation
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

`UserOnlyStore<...>.CreateUserPasskey(TUser user, UserPasskeyInfo passkey)` (and the identical
override in `UserStore.cs`) maps every property from `UserPasskeyInfo` onto the new
`TUserPasskey.Data` except `Aaguid`. As a result, the AAGUID captured during passkey
registration (`PasskeyHandler.cs`, set from `attestedCredentialData.Aaguid`) is discarded
and stored as null in the database.

Read paths are unaffected — `IdentityUserPasskeyExtensions.ToUserPasskeyInfo()` correctly
maps `passkey.Data.Aaguid` back — so authenticator identification (e.g. showing "Windows
Hello", "1Password", etc. via `PasskeyAuthenticators.TryGetDefaultDisplayName`) silently
fails for any passkey created through the EF Core store, since `Aaguid` is always null.

### Expected Behavior

`Aaguid` should be persisted, matching the other passkey fields.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a Blazor Web App with `-au Individual` on .NET 11.
2. Register a new passkey.
3. Inspect `AspNetUserPasskeys` (or call `GetPasskeysAsync`) — `Aaguid` is null even though
   the authenticator provided one during attestation.

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128

### Anything else?

_No response_

Issues.Title: BlazorWebTemplate_ConditionalPasskeyRegistration reads response body after navigation
Issues.Body:
## Description

`BlazorWebTemplate_ConditionalPasskeyRegistration` intermittently fails on Windows because the test reads a Playwright `IResponse` body after the page has navigated away from that response.

The generated application appears to complete the passkey flow correctly. The failure occurs later while the test inspects the captured HTML response.

## Failure

```text
Microsoft.Playwright.PlaywrightException: Protocol error (Network.getResponseBody): No resource with given identifier found
Response body is not available for a response that was navigated away from. Read response.body() before triggering any navigation.

   at Microsoft.Playwright.Core.Response.BodyAsync()
   at Microsoft.Playwright.Core.Response.TextAsync()
   at BlazorTemplates.Tests.BlazorWebTemplateTest.BlazorWebTemplate_ConditionalPasskeyRegistration(...)
      in /_/src/ProjectTemplates/test/Templates.Blazor.Tests/BlazorWebTemplateTest.cs:line 266
```

The failing line is:

```csharp
var redisplayedPage = await upgradeResponse.TextAsync();
```

## Observed failures

| Build | PR | Theory case |
|---|---|---|
| [1610717](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1610717&view=logs&j=6c33d704-163a-5170-38fa-caa7bc99f17c&t=a59c73d3-09b1-5a7e-4e53-9d83598ad56e) | #69441 | `Failure / Success` |
| [1610395](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1610395&view=logs&j=6c33d704-163a-5170-38fa-caa7bc99f17c&t=a59c73d3-09b1-5a7e-4e53-9d83598ad56e) | #69461 | `DatabaseFailure / Success` |
| [1608370](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1608370&view=logs&j=6c33d704-163a-5170-38fa-caa7bc99f17c&t=a59c73d3-09b1-5a7e-4e53-9d83598ad56e) | #67553 | `Failure / Success` |
| [1607585](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1607585&view=logs&j=6c33d704-163a-5170-38fa-caa7bc99f17c&t=a59c73d3-09b1-5a7e-4e53-9d83598ad56e) | #69422 | `Failure / Unsupported` |

For builds 1610395 and 1608370, the published `Templates.Blazor.Tests_net11.0_x64.xml` contains 27 tests with 26 passing and this as the only failure.

## Cause

The test captures the first `/Account/PasskeyUpgrade` response, but does not read its body immediately:

```csharp
var upgradeResponseTask = page.WaitForResponseAsync(...);
await page.GetByRole(...).ClickAsync();
var upgradeResponse = await upgradeResponseTask;
await page.WaitForURLAsync(returnUrl, ...);
```

The browser then performs another upgrade request and navigates back to `returnUrl`. The test performs additional page and server-state checks before finally calling `upgradeResponse.TextAsync()`. Chromium can discard the original response body once navigation occurs, producing `Network.getResponseBody: No resource with given identifier found`.

A representative successful server sequence before the exception is:

```text
POST /Account/PasskeyUpgrade -> 200 text/html
POST /Account/PasskeyUpgrade -> 302
GET /auth?... -> 200 text/html
GET /test/passkeys -> 200 application/json
Network.getResponseBody fails while reading the earlier 200 response
```

This test and ordering were introduced in #68194. The affected builds belong to unrelated PRs, supporting that this is a shared test race rather than a product regression in those PRs.

## Suggested fix

Read and retain the response text immediately after `upgradeResponseTask` completes and before waiting for or triggering subsequent navigation. Use the retained string for the later assertions.

Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug


When static files are served by using `MapStaticAssets` method, served files has improper cache headers.

1. For `/index.html` when served as a fallback (`MapFallbackToFile`) response does not include `Cache-Control: no-cache` resulting in caching the result by most browsers. As a result leading to bugs when a new version is released.
Also, non compressed file is served even so browser send `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br`.
2. For `/index-[Hash].js` files (or `.css` files), response contains `Cache-Control: no-cache` prohibiting browsers to cache immutable file.

### Expected Behavior

1. For `/index.html` when served as a fallback - response should have `Cache-Control: no-cache` header forcing browsers to check for a fresh version each time when the page is requested. Ideally make it configurable.
Also, compressed files should be served when possible.
2. For files with fingerprints (e.g. `/index-[Hash].js`) include `Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, immutable`. Allow specifying 


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a new solution based on the **Vue and ASP.NET Core** a project template as described [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/javascript/tutorial-asp-net-core-with-vue?view=visualstudio#publish-the-project)
2. Run it and inspect response properties of requests to '/' or '/assets/index-DAMbWbfh.js'.

_No response_

10.0.400

I tried to override cache settings by adding next block under `<Project>` in my `Server.csproj` file.

  <ItemGroup>

Issues.Title: Order root component operations without serializing circuit batches
Issues.Body:
## Why
`UpdateRootComponents` batches can overlap when lifecycle handlers, inbound middleware, rendering, or client acknowledgments yield. A dependent batch could apply its operations before its predecessor had even invoked Add/Update/Remove. Serializing entire batches would fix that ordering but unnecessarily make later batches wait for rendering, post-`next()` middleware, or a slow client acknowledgment.

Fixes #59657.

## What changed
- On the renderer dispatcher, each batch captures the previous batch's **operations-applied** task and installs its own `TaskCompletionSource` with asynchronous continuations. It awaits its predecessor without blocking the dispatcher. The barrier completes immediately after Add/Update/Remove have been invoked, or after inbound middleware returns without invoking `next()`; it does not wait for rendering, quiescence, post-`next()` middleware, or acknowledgment.
- A failure before operations are applied faults the barrier, so queued batches do not apply operations. The first failure marks the circuit errored, follows the existing log / `UnhandledException` / client-error flow, and causes circuit termination through `CircuitRegistry`. Later batches skip operations and do not report the same error again. If a batch fails *after* releasing its barrier, operations already started by another batch may finish; subsequent batches still see the errored state and do not start operations.
- Preserve successful acknowledgment behavior and state-store cleanup. No lock, bounded queue, disposal cancellation, or whole-batch serialization is introduced.

## Validation
- Targeted Server build via `eng/build.cmd`: succeeded with zero warnings/errors.
- `dotnet test src\Components\Server\test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Tests.csproj --no-build --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~CircuitHostTest|FullyQualifiedName~CircuitRegistryTest' -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false`: **80 passed**.
- Before the failure-propagation fix, both lifecycle/inbound failure test rows applied a successor's root component, and a post-`next()` failure allowed a later batch to apply; each failed at the expected assertion and passed with the fix. A gated-acknowledgment regression likewise showed a short-circuited batch previously held its successor until acknowledgment, and passes now.

Issues.Title: Fix AG-UI Dojo sample to use ChatOptions.Tools instead of UIActionBlock
Issues.Body:
Fixes #69469

### Description

In the AG-UI Dojo sample, `AgenticChatScenario` previously relied on `AutoInvokeAction.razor` and a custom `BlockRenderer<UIActionBlock>` to simulate frontend tool execution. `UIActionBlock` is intended for human-in-the-loop (HITL) scenarios requiring user intervention before execution resumes, rather than automated client-side tool execution.

This PR refactors the scenario to use standard `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` / AG-UI client tool patterns:

* The tool is registered directly on `options.ChatOptions.Tools` as an `AIFunction` via `AIFunctionFactory.Create`.
* Tool invocations are processed within the agent chat pipeline, executing locally on Blazor's synchronization context and returning execution output back to the model history.
* A typed AG-UI tool block (`ChangeBackgroundToolBlock`) and corresponding renderer (`ChangeBackgroundCard`) surface tool execution feedback in the chat message list, matching the existing `WeatherToolBlock` / `WeatherCard` reference pattern.

### Changes

* **Replaced `AutoInvokeAction.razor`:** Deleted the obsolete component and replaced the ad-hoc action block with a typed AG-UI tool block workflow.
* **Registered native client tool:** Added `change_background` to `options.ChatOptions.Tools` via `AIFunctionFactory.Create(ChangeBackground, ...)`.
* **Synchronous UI mutation:** Implemented synchronous `ChangeBackground` to update `_background` and invoke `StateHasChanged()` directly within Blazor's synchronization context.
* **Added custom tool block & card renderer:**
* Created `ChangeBackgroundToolBlock.cs` (`[ToolBlock("change_background")]` deriving from `FunctionInvocationContentBlock`) with parameter mappings and computed value resolution.
* Created `ChangeBackgroundCard.razor` and scoped `ChangeBackgroundCard.razor.css` to render execution status (`"The background was changed to {value}"`).
* Registered the block renderer in `AgenticChatScenario.razor` inside `<MessageListContent>` and called `options.AddGeneratedToolBlocks()`.


* **Cleaned up orphaned styles:** Removed legacy `.agentic-chat__action-status` styles from `app.css` in favor of component-scoped CSS.
* **Updated E2E tests (`AgenticChatScenarioTests.cs`):**
* Replaced the obsolete `.agentic-chat__action-status` assertion with an assertion verifying `.change-background-card` contains the confirmation message.
* Preserved checks for `data-background`, inline styles on `.agentic-chat`, and assistant turn continuation.


* **Preserved HITL sample:** Left `PredictiveStateUpdatesScenario.razor` untouched as the canonical demonstration of interactive `UIActionBlock` workflows.

### Testing

* `dotnet build src/Components/AI/testassets/DojoClient/DojoClient.csproj` (0 warnings, 0 errors).
* Ran `DojoClient.E2E.Tests`:
* `AgenticChatScenarioTests` (5/5 passed)
* `PredictiveStateUpdatesScenarioTests` (1/1 passed)

Issues.Title: Blazor Server: a server-initiated NavigateTo whose interop reply is lost during a transient disconnect terminates the reconnected circuit one minute later
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

No open one. #45267 (closed by #53297, shipped in 8.0.2) added the catch in `RemoteNavigationManager.PerformNavigationAsync` for a circuit that is **permanently disconnected** (the browser has left). This report is the other case: the browser has **not** left — the circuit is disconnected and retained, or has already reconnected — and the same timeout terminates it.

### Describe the bug

On Interactive Server, `NavigationManager.NavigateTo` sends a `navigateTo` JS-interop call and awaits its reply with no cancellation token (`RemoteNavigationManager.PerformNavigationAsync`, v10.0.12 `src/Components/Server/src/Circuits/RemoteNavigationManager.cs:136`), so the only bound is `CircuitOptions.JSInteropDefaultCallTimeout` (one minute).

If the SignalR connection is down when the call is issued, `DefaultHubLifetimeManager.SendConnectionAsync` discards the message for the missing connection and returns a completed task; nothing re-sends it after the reconnect (render batches are replayed, interop calls are not). If the connection is up but the browser's reply is lost, the result is the same.

One minute later the pending call is cancelled. The cancellation is swallowed only when `RemoteJSRuntime.IsPermanentlyDisconnected` (`:139-143`), which only `CircuitHost.DisposeAsync` sets. A circuit that is merely disconnected and retained (within `DisconnectedCircuitRetentionPeriod`), or that has since **reconnected**, takes the generic branch (`:144-150`): `Navigation failed when changing the location to ...` (RemoteNavigationManager event 4), `UnhandledException`, `Unhandled exception in circuit` (CircuitHost event 111), `JS.Error` to the live browser, and `CircuitRegistry.TerminateAsync`. The user, whose page had recovered and was interactive again, sees the "unhandled error" banner and must reload.

The application cannot defend itself with the public API: `NavigateTo` takes no token, returns before the failure, and exposes nothing to observe it.

### Expected Behavior

Either the navigation request survives a reconnect (re-issued, or the pending call completes when the connection returns), or a lost reply is reported to the application without terminating a circuit that is still live — and there is a supported way to navigate after an awaited operation with a bound the application controls.

### Steps To Reproduce

Minimal reproduction (no third-party components, authentication or database): `https://github.com/DevonEast/blazor-server-navigateto-reconnect-timeout`

Automated (about 2–3 minutes, exit code 0 means reproduced):

```powershell
dotnet build App
dotnet build Driver
pwsh Driver/bin/Debug/net10.0/playwright.ps1 install chromium   # once
dotnet run --project Driver
```

Manual: `dotnet run --project App`, open the page, click **Save**, use DevTools to go offline for about 10 seconds during the 5-second operation, then go back online. The reconnect dialog clears and the page shows "saved … navigating" without moving to `/done`. About a minute after the click the page shows the unhandled-error banner; the server console shows the sequence below.

Recorded run (`repro-output.txt` in the repository): disconnect at 1.8 s, navigation requested while disconnected at 6.3 s, reconnect to the same circuit at 6.8 s, page still rendered and interactive, events 4 and 111 at 66.3 s, circuit removed, banner visible.

### Exceptions (if any)

```
fail: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits.RemoteNavigationManager[4]
      Navigation failed when changing the location to /done
      System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException: A task was canceled.
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits.RemoteNavigationManager.PerformNavigationAsync()
fail: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits.CircuitHost[111]
      Unhandled exception in circuit '...'.
      System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException: A task was canceled.
```

### .NET Version

SDK 10.0.401; `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` 10.0.12 (`dotnet --list-runtimes`). Reproduction driver: Microsoft.Playwright 1.62.0, Chromium.

### Anything else?

- Source read at v10.0.12: `RemoteNavigationManager.cs:124-151` (no token at `:136`; the `IsPermanentlyDisconnected` filter at `:139-143`); `CircuitHost.cs:235` (the only place the flag is set); `DefaultHubLifetimeManager.cs:183-191` (the discarded send).
- Same outcome for both loss orderings: the call issued after the hub registered the drop, and the call issued into a connection the hub still believed up (the keep-alive timeout registers the drop later).
- Practical impact and our workaround, to be clear that it is an application-side mitigation and not a fix of the framework behaviour: the application we maintain now navigates after awaited operations through the public `Blazor.navigateTo` export with its own bounded interop call, confirmed by `NavigationManager.LocationChanged`, keeping the result on screen with a link when the confirmation does not arrive. That keeps the session alive, but it relies on an export that is not documented on Learn, it leaves the framework's one-minute unbounded await in place for any application that simply calls `NavigateTo`, and it has its own residual (a request delivered late after the user has left and returned to the same address still navigates).
- Questions: is the recovered-circuit termination intended? What is the supported way to navigate after an awaited operation so a request or reply lost in a transient disconnect does not end the session?

Issues.Title: Remember me isPersistent understanding
Issues.Body:
This is more of a question but its not enough of a question that i could post it up on stack overflow without risking it just getting closed as primary opinion based or to broad.   So i am going to put it here in hopes of getting an answer.

The issue is the understanding of how remember me is supposed to work.    My problem is that its not doing what we would expect it to do.   

Management expects when a user logs in and clicks remember me that they will then not be required to type their login and password again for a month.  Whether or not they will still have to type in the 2fa code is up for debate.

What is actually happening is that i can close the browser reboot and come back for about an hour and 15 minutes and then i will be forced to type my password again.    This still happens even with a valid `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie set that is not due to expire for another month.

After digging around in the code i found that Remember me is actually isPersistent and it is defined as.

>Flag indicating whether the sign-in cookie should persist after the browser is closed.

Which brings you to:

There are two different types of Cookies:

- session cookies, held in memory, and which expire once the browser exits
- persistent cookies, which have a time-to-live, are persisted on disk, and are sent by the browser until their time-to-live has elapsed.

All this being said remember machine 2fa works as expected i am not prompted again for the 2fa and i have a cookie on my machine `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`.

So I guess my question is why are we not getting a `Identity.FactorRememberMe` or why isn't sign in respecting a long life time of the `AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie?

How is this supposed to work exactly?   I am following the code here even though we have normal MVC and not razor pages like you have in the example.  I am still just calling 

>var signInUserResult = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(userName, password, rememberMe, true);

Note: I am using Asp .net Identity in Identity server 4 application.

Issues.Title: Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?
Issues.Body:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.identity.entityframeworkcore.identityuser?view=aspnetcore-1.1

I'm looking through various implementations from the [readme](https://github.com/aspnet/Identity/blob/master/README.md) and I've noticed they all use `IdentityUser ` for their concrete type to pass to `UserManager`, or have had to craft a custom type to be able to have a contract between the database and the .NET AspNetIdentity implentation they've written (see the DynamoDB library).

I've had to do this too for the [Marten implementation I've written](https://github.com/yetanotherchris/Marten.AspNetIdentity), and the reason is, a `TUser` that your `UserStore` takes, should really be an interface - it will always have an email, most likely an Id of some sort, firstname, lastname and then a bag of properties.

Things become even more abstract when dealing with claims.

If everyone is using `IdentityUser` or their own custom `TUser` doesn't this defeat the purpose of AspnetIdentity - which is to be able to switch and change implementations easily? That isn't possible if your consumer is tightly coupled with a `TUser` implementation of the library.

### Example `TUser` implementations

- [MongoIdentityUser](https://github.com/tugberkugurlu/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/MongoIdentityUser.cs)
- [DynamoIdentityUser](https://github.com/miltador/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/DynamoIdentityUser.cs)
- [Redis uses `IdentityUser<string>`](https://github.com/aguacongas/Identity.Redis/blob/develop/src/Aguacongas.Identity.Redis/UserStore.cs)

3. Creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 will always install the .NET Core 1.0/1.1 web tooling, and this is not necessary when previous reason has reached the unsupported period and it's quite near or might be the same time of VS 2019 release.

Therefore for those that still need to maintain ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 projects, we could use VS 2017 as long as the VS 2017 is still in support lifecycle or in mainstream support lifecycle.

I welcome feedback 🙂

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the OpenID Connect handler validates the signed ID token `auth_time` claim whenever `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge` causes an effective `max_age` value to be sent.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69321 and addresses https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67462.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

The handler sent `max_age` on the authorization request but did not validate the returned ID token's `auth_time`. Applications relied entirely on the identity provider to honor the request. A missing, malformed, stale, or excessively future `auth_time` did not cause authentication to fail.

### New behavior

When an effective `max_age` is sent, the handler correlates the exact value through protected authorization-transaction state and validates every ID token used by the supported authorization flow after normal token and OpenID Connect protocol validation.

The `auth_time` claim must be an integral, nonnegative OpenID Connect NumericDate. Authentication fails when the claim is missing, malformed, fractional, negative, overflowed, later than the current time plus `OpenIdConnectOptions.TokenValidationParameters.ClockSkew`, or older than `max_age` plus that clock skew. Exact boundaries and values within skew are accepted.

The validation covers authorization-code, implicit, and hybrid flows, including both relevant ID tokens in hybrid flows, and both the default `TokenHandler` path and legacy `SecurityTokenValidator` path. No validation occurs when no `max_age` is configured. In addition to the `MaxAge` properties, applications can configure the parameter through `AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` or `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

OpenID Connect Core requires the authorization server to include `auth_time` when `max_age` is requested and recommends that the relying party validate it. Correlating and checking the signed assertion prevents a missing or nonconforming assertion from silently satisfying an application's configured maximum authentication age.

The guarantee remains limited to the trusted identity provider's signed assertion. ASP.NET Core cannot prove that a particular physical authentication ceremony occurred and cannot protect against a compromised identity provider that signs false data. This change does not revalidate UserInfo, refresh-token redemption, local cookie lifetime, or physical user interaction.

### Recommended action

Ensure that identity providers emit a valid signed `auth_time` and honor the requested `max_age` whenever the application configures that parameter, most commonly through `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`.

For a temporarily incompatible provider, restore the previous request-only behavior by setting the process-wide compatibility switch before authentication starts:

```csharp
AppContext.SetSwitch(
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation",
    true);
```

The equivalent runtime configuration is:

```json
{
  "runtimeOptions": {
    "configProperties": {
      "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation": true
    }
  }
}
```

The switch defaults to `false` and is intended only as a temporary provider-compatibility escape hatch.

When pushed authorization is used, set or modify `max_age` in `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`. Changing it later in `OnPushAuthorization` is rejected while validation is active unless pushing is skipped, because the handler has already correlated the value with the authorization response.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. The behavioral change affects applications that set:

- `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectOptions.AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` when it includes `max_age`
- `OpenIdConnectEvents.OnRedirectToIdentityProvider` when it sets `max_age`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time" (#537)

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Identity external login keys use ordinal equality
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the built-in Entity Framework Core Identity stores verify external-login `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values using managed ordinal equality after the indexed database lookup returns a candidate.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69277.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

`UserStore` and `UserOnlyStore` filtered external logins with a database-translated equality predicate. The database collation therefore determined whether the stored `(LoginProvider, ProviderKey)` tuple matched the supplied values.

On a case-insensitive collation, `FindByLoginAsync` could resolve a login whose provider name or provider key differed only by case. On databases where equality ignores trailing spaces, it could also resolve a key that differed by trailing spaces. `RemoveLoginAsync` used the same collation-dependent lookup and could remove such a login.

### New behavior

The database equality remains the indexed candidate lookup. The built-in EF Identity stores then require the returned `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` to match the requested values using `StringComparison.Ordinal`.

A collation-only match now causes `FindByLoginAsync` to return no user and `RemoveLoginAsync` to perform no removal. Exact ordinal matches continue to work.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

External provider keys are opaque identifiers whose equality must not vary with the configured database provider or collation. Managed ordinal verification makes the built-in EF stores consistent with the in-memory reference store while preserving the existing indexed database lookup.

### Recommended action

Ensure that applications persist and later supply the exact `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values issued for an external login. Do not normalize, case-fold, trim, or otherwise alter provider keys.

Third-party `IUserLoginStore<TUser>` implementations own their equality semantics. Implementations that query a collation-aware database should preserve an indexed candidate lookup and verify the materialized provider name and key with ordinal equality before resolving or removing a login.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. This behavioral change affects the built-in Entity Framework Core implementations of:

- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.FindByLoginAsync`
- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.RemoveLoginAsync`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Blazor server-side rendering defers antiforgery validation to middleware
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, Blazor static server-side rendering (SSR) endpoints no longer validate antiforgery tokens themselves. They rely on the antiforgery verdict recorded by upstream middleware and generate antiforgery tokens only when token-based antiforgery middleware is present.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67082.

### Version

.NET 11 Preview 6

### Previous behavior

When a Blazor SSR endpoint handled a form `POST`, the endpoint validated the request itself if antiforgery middleware hadn't already recorded a result.

The endpoint also generated and stored antiforgery tokens for rendered forms even when `app.UseAntiforgery()` wasn't present in the pipeline.

Consequently, apps that didn't call `app.UseAntiforgery()` still emitted and validated antiforgery tokens.

### New behavior

Blazor SSR endpoints now trust the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` verdict recorded by upstream middleware. A form `POST` is rejected with `400 Bad Request` when the recorded verdict is invalid.

The verdict can be recorded by:

- Token-based antiforgery middleware added by `app.UseAntiforgery()` (explicit usage).
- Automatic cross-origin CSRF protection middleware added by default to apps built with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder`.

Blazor SSR endpoints no longer call `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync` directly. Antiforgery tokens are generated only when token-based antiforgery middleware ran for the request.

Apps using `app.UseAntiforgery()` retain token-based validation. Apps without it rely on automatic cross-origin CSRF protection and no longer emit antiforgery tokens for their forms.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Token-based antiforgery and automatic cross-origin CSRF protection now record a shared verdict through `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature`.

Validating again inside the Blazor SSR endpoint duplicated work and could produce a result different from the middleware verdict. Generating tokens without token-based antiforgery middleware also produced tokens that nothing validated.

### Recommended action

If your Blazor SSR app relies on antiforgery tokens for form validation or rendering, ensure that it calls `app.UseAntiforgery()`:
```csharp
var app = builder.Build();

app.UseAntiforgery();
```

If you were not calling `app.UseAntiforgery()` before you will start using CSRF protection as the defense mechanism from now on.

### Affected APIs

None. This is a behavioral change affecting Blazor SSR form processing and antiforgery-token generation.

# ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach end of support on April 13, 2027

> Update: The ASP.NET Core 2.3 end of support date was updated from April 7, 2027 to April 13, 2027 to align with the Microsoft servicing release cycles.

Today we are announcing that ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach **end of support on April 13, 2027**. After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide security patches, bug fixes, or technical support for ASP.NET Core 2.3.

This announcement provides the required 12 months of advance notice, as defined by the [Microsoft Support Lifecycle Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/lifecycle/faq/general-lifecycle#what-is-the-lifecycle-policy-for-tools-) for products classified as "Tools."

## Current support policy

Issues.Body:
Automates creation of documentation tracking issues in `dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs` when breaking change issues are opened or labeled in this repository.

**New workflow:** `.github/workflows/create-docs-issue.yaml`

- Creates issue in docs repo with:
  - Title: `[Breaking Change] <original title>`

- Posts comment on source issue with link to docs issue

Multi-layer detection to handle race conditions and partial failures:
- Checks for existing bot comments in source issue
- Searches docs repo by title before creating

Separate try-catch blocks for each operation:
- Comment listing failures → proceed with search

- Comment posting failures → don't fail workflow (docs issue already created)
- Permission errors → explicit message about `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` requirement

Configure `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` repository secret with `repo` scope for cross-repository issue creation. Falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` but will fail with clear error message.

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Deprecating WebHostBuilder,  IWebHost, and WebHost
Issues.Body:
### Description

`WebHostBuilder` was replaced by `HostBuilder` ([generic host](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder)) in 3.0 and we also added [`WebApplicationBuilder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) in 6.0.

We are now marking `WebHostBuilder` as obsolete to encourage users to move on to the alternatives which is where future investments will occur, and we're also marking `IWebHost` and `WebHost` as deprecated to clean up other parts of the now obsolete web host story.

### Version

.NET 10 RC 1

### Previous behavior

```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

### New behavior

Using `WebHostBuilder` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR004**:
> warning ASPDEPR004: WebHostBuilder is deprecated in favor of HostBuilder and WebApplicationBuilder. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/004.

Using `IWebHost` or `WebHost` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR008**:
> warning ASPDEPR008: WebHost is obsolete. Use HostBuilder or WebApplicationBuilder instead. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/008.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [x] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

We recommend the use of `HostBuilder` and `WebApplication` going forward over `WebHostBuilder` because they have all the features of `WebHostBuilder` and will be the focus of future investment.

### Recommended action

See https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/host/generic-host or https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/minimal-apis/webapplication for more details on the different hosting models. As well as [HostBuilder replaces WebHostBuilder](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder) and [Introducing WebApplication](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) for migration guides.

Below is an example of converting `WebHostBuilder` to `HostBuilder`:

**Before**
```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

**After**
```csharp
using var host = new HostBuilder()
    .ConfigureWebHost(webHostBuilder =>
    {
        webHostBuilder
            .UseTestServer() // If using TestServer
            .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
            .UseStartup()
            .UseKestrel();
    })
    .Build();
await host.StartAsync();

var testServer = host.GetTestServer();
```

Both Copilot and ChatGpt have given good results so far when asked to convert a WebHostBuilder example to use HostBuilder. Below is an example prompt:
<details>
<summary>Example AI Prompt</summary>

> Can you convert
>
> var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
>     .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
>     .UseStartup()
>     .UseKestrel();
> // Test code might use TestServer:
> var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
>
> to use HostBuilder.

</details>

### Affected APIs

`public class Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.WebHostBuilder`
`public interface Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.IWebHost`
`public static class Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebHost`

### Discussion

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/63480

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Exception diagnostics are suppressed when `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns true
Issues.Body:
### Description

The [ASP.NET Core exception handler middleware](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#exception-handler-page), `UseExceptionHandler()`, is responsible for catching and processing unhandled exceptions from ASP.NET Core requests.

In .NET 8, we introduced [`IExceptionHandler`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#iexceptionhandler). Implementations of `IExceptionHandler` are registered with dependency injection and invoked by the middleware. An implementation can return `true` from `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` to indicate that the exception has been handled. The middleware stops processing the exception once it has been handled.

In .NET 10, we're changing the default behavior so that the middleware no longer records diagnostics for exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

### Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

### Previous behavior

The exception handler middleware recorded diagnostics about exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

The exception diagnostics are:

- Logging `UnhandledException` to `ILogger`.
- Writing the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HandledException` event to `EventSource`.
- Adding the `error.type` tag to the `http.server.request.duration` metric.

### New behavior

If `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns `true`, then exception diagnostics are no longer recorded by default.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

ASP.NET Core users have given feedback that the previous behavior was undesirable. Their `IExceptionHandler` implementation reported that the exception was handled, but the error handling middleware still recorded the error in the app's telemetry.

We are changing ASP.NET Core to follow the behavior expected by users by suppressing diagnostics when `IExceptionHandler` handles the exception. We're also adding configuration options to customize exception diagnostics behavior if needed.

### Recommended action

If you want handled exceptions to continue recording telemetry, you can use the new `ExceptionHandlerOptions.SuppressDiagnosticsCallback` option:

```cs
app.UseExceptionHandler(new ExceptionHandlerOptions
{
    SuppressDiagnosticsCallback = context => false;
});
```

The context passed to the callback includes information about the exception, the request, and whether the exception was handled. Returning `false` from the callback indicates that diagnostics shouldn't be suppressed. This restores the previous behavior.

### References

- Issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54554
- PR: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/59074

### Affected APIs

- `UseExceptionHandler()`
- `IExceptionHandler`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and MVC API analyzers are deprecated
Issues.Body:
## Description

The `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` MSBuild property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. When `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will now emit warning `ASPDEPR007`.

## Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

## Previous behavior

Previously, developers could set `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` in their Web SDK projects to enable MVC API analyzers without any warnings or deprecation notices.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net9.0</TargetFramework>
    <IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

The project would build successfully without any deprecation warnings.

## New behavior

Starting in .NET 10 Preview 7, when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will emit warning `ASPDEPR007`:

```
warning ASPDEPR007: The IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
```

The analyzers will continue to function, but developers will receive this deprecation warning during compilation.

## Type of breaking change

- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

## Reason for change

## Reason for change

The MVC API analyzers were originally introduced to help keep return types and attributes in sync for API controllers, ensuring consistency between method signatures and their corresponding OpenAPI documentation. These analyzers provided compile-time validation to catch mismatches between declared return types and the actual types returned by controller actions.

However, with the introduction of Minimal APIs and the `TypedResults` pattern, the .NET ecosystem has evolved toward a more type-safe approach for API development. `TypedResults` provides compile-time guarantees about response types without requiring additional analyzers, making the MVC API analyzers redundant for modern .NET applications. In .NET 10, `TypedResults` are supported in controller-based APIs.

**Previous approach with MVC API analyzers:**
```csharp
[HttpGet]
[ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)]
[ProducesResponseType(404)]
public async Task<ActionResult> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    if (product == null)
        return NotFound(); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType(404)
    
    return Ok(product); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)
}
```

**Or with controller actions using TypedResults:**
```csharp
[HttpGet("{id}")]
public async Task<Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    return product == null 
        ? TypedResults.NotFound() 
        : TypedResults.Ok(product);
}
```

The `TypedResults` pattern eliminates the need for separate analyzers because the return type itself (`Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>`) explicitly declares all possible response types at compile time. This approach is more maintainable, provides better IntelliSense support, and automatically generates accurate OpenAPI documentation without additional tooling.

As the .NET ecosystem continues to embrace `TypedResults` as the recommended pattern for API development, the MVC API analyzers have become obsolete and are being deprecated to streamline the development experience.

## Recommended action

Developers should:

1. **Remove the deprecated property**: Remove `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` from your project files to eliminate the warning.

2. **Suppress the warning temporarily**: If you need to continue using the deprecated analyzers temporarily, you can suppress the warning:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);ASPDEPR007</NoWarn>
</PropertyGroup>
```

3. **Migrate to TypedResults**: Migrate to the `TypedResults` pattern documented above to ensure better consistency between application behavior and OpenAPI documentation.

## Affected APIs

- MSBuild property: `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers`
- Associated MVC API analyzers included when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is `true`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Forwarded Headers Middleware Now Ignores X-Forwarded-* Headers from Unknown Proxies
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 8.0.17 and 9.0.6, the Forwarded Headers Middleware will ignore all `X-Forwarded-*` headers from proxies that are not explicitly configured as trusted.

### Version

.NET 8

### Previous behavior

Previously, the middleware, when not configured to use `X-Forwarded-For`, would process `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and `X-Forwarded-Host` headers from any source, potentially allowing malicious or misconfigured proxies/clients to spoof these headers and affect your application's understanding of client information.

### New behavior

With this change, only headers sent by known, trusted proxies (as configured via `ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownProxies` and `ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownNetworks`) will be processed. Headers from unknown sources will be ignored.

**This is a breaking change**: If your deployment relied on forwarded headers from proxies not configured in your application's trusted proxy list, those headers will no longer be honored.

This can cause behavior like infinite redirects if you're using the Https redirection middleware and using TLS termination in your proxy. Or authentication to fail if using TLS termination and expecting an https request.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

The change was made for security hardening, as the proxy and IP lists weren't being applied in all cases.

### Recommended action

- **Review your deployment topology:**  
  Ensure that all legitimate proxy servers in front of your app are properly added to `KnownProxies` or `KnownNetworks` in your `ForwardedHeadersOptions` configuration.
  ```csharp
  app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions
  {
      KnownProxies = { IPAddress.Parse("YOUR_PROXY_IP") }
  });
  ```
  Or, for a network:
  ```csharp
  app.UseForwardedHeaders(new ForwardedHeadersOptions
  {
      KnownNetworks = { new IPNetwork(IPAddress.Parse("YOUR_NETWORK_IP"), PREFIX_LENGTH) }
  });
  ```

- **If you wish to enable previous behavior:**  
  You may need to relax your configuration, but this is **not recommended** due to security risks. You can do this by clearing the `KnownNetworks` and `KnownProxies` lists in `ForwardedHeadersOptions` to allow any proxy or network to forward these headers.

You can also set the `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` environment variable to true, which clears the lists and enables `ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto`.

For applications targeting .NET 9.0 or less, you can set the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides.IgnoreUnknownProxiesWithoutFor` [AppContext](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/runtime-libraries/system-appcontext) switch to `"true"` or `1` to get back to the previous behavior. Alternatively, set the `MICROSOFT_ASPNETCORE_HTTPOVERRIDES_IGNORE_UNKNOWN_PROXIES_WITHOUT_FOR` environment variable.

> [!Note]
> In cloud environments, the proxy IP(s) can change over the lifetime of the app and `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED` is sometimes used to make forwarded headers work.

### References
